test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Electronic Mechanic) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following types of errors can be minimised by proper instrument calibration?
solution:
Proper **instrument calibration** is done to correct consistent deviations caused by the instrument itself.

 
• 
 
**Systematic errors** arise due to faulty calibration, zero error, aging of components, or environmental effects.

 
 
• 
 
Calibration adjusts the instrument to reduce these **predictable and repeatable errors**.

 
 
• 
 
Random, observational, and gross errors are mainly due to human factors or unpredictable variations and cannot be eliminated by calibration.
